lesson_title: Be Your Own Harshest Critic, Then Say It First
hook_text: The team that admits the string slipped beats the team that pretends it did not. Here is why.
clip_script: Evaluation day. Your list of musts from Week 6 becomes a list of tests. Must lift 500 grams to 250 millimetres? Hang it, crank it, measure it. Must not topple when pushed? Push it. Each one: met, partly met, not met, and what you saw. Then three paragraphs. What worked and why. What fell short and what caused it: the string slipped because the axle was smooth. What you would change: a card collar on the axle. Honest beats perfect, every time, because the examiner is marking your thinking, not your luck. Then presentation day. Tell the story in order: problem, research, design, build, test, improve. Everyone speaks. Show the model turning. Point at the drawing, do not read it. And if it breaks in front of everyone? Say why, say the fix, keep going. You already knew. That is what engineers do.
visual_style: Whiteboard table fills with ticks, a half-tick and a cross; three short paragraphs appear; then a stick-figure team at the front with a poster, a model turning, one figure steadying it.
pacing: Evaluation in thirty seconds, presentation in thirty, closing on the failure-handled-well beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the three evaluation paragraphs for your own model.
